{{short description|Italian physicist}}
'''Andrea Cavalleri''' (born 1969) is an [[Italian language|Italian]] [[physicist]] who specializes in [[optical science]] and in [[condensed matter physics]]. He is the founding director of the {{Ill|Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter|lt=|de|Max-Planck-Institut für Struktur und Dynamik der Materie}} in [[Hamburg, Germany]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mpsd.mpg.de/|title=Startseite|website=www.mpsd.mpg.de}}</ref> and a professor of Physics at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www2.physics.ox.ac.uk/contacts/people/cavalleri|title=Andrea Cavalleri &#124; University of Oxford Department of Physics|website=www2.physics.ox.ac.uk}}</ref> He was awarded the 2018 [[Frank Isakson Prize for Optical Effects in Solids|Frank Isakson Prize]] for his pioneering work on [[Ultrafast laser spectroscopy|ultrafast optical spectroscopy]] applied to [[Condensed matter physics|condensed matter]] systems.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=2018 Frank Isakson Prize for Optical Effects in Solids Recipient|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Cavalleri&first_nm=Andrea&year=2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210214134325/https://aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm%3DAndrea%26last_nm%3DCavalleri%26year%3D2018 |archive-date=2021-02-14 |access-date=2020-06-28|website=American Physical Society|language=en}}</ref>

==Scientific achievements==
Cavalleri is known for his application of light to create new states of matter, and especially for the use of [[Terahertz radiation|terahertz]] and mid-infrared optical pulses to sculpt new crystal structures. The field of research pioneered by Cavalleri is sometimes referred to as [[non-linear phononics]].<ref>M. Först, C. Manzoni, S. Kaiser, Y. Tomioka, Y. Tokura, R. Merlin, and A. Cavalleri: ''Nonlinear phononics as an ultrafast route to lattice control.'' In: ''Nature Physics'' 7, 854-856 (2011), DOI: https://dx.doi.org/10.1038/nphys2055</ref><ref>R. Mankowsky, A. Subedi, M. Först, S. O. Mariager, M. Chollet, H. T. Lemke, J. S. Robinson, J. M. Glownia, M. P. Minitti, A. Frano, M. Fechner, N. A. Spaldin, T. Loew, B. Keimer, A. Georges, and A. Cavalleri: ''Nonlinear lattice dynamics as a basis for enhanced superconductivity in YBa<sub>2</sub>Cu<sub>3</sub>O<sub>6.5</sub>.'' In: ''Nature'' 516, 71-73 (2014),  DOI: https://dx.doi.org/10.1038/nature13875</ref>

He has shown that phononic control can be used to create new crystal structures with light, to induce hidden metallic states in oxides,<ref>M. Rini, R. Tobey, N. Dean, J. Itatani, Y. Tomioka, Y. Tokura, R. W. Schoenlein, and A. Cavalleri: ''Control of the electronic phase of a manganite by mode-selective vibrational excitation.'' In: ''Nature'' 449, 72-74 (2007), DOI: https://dx.doi.org/10.1038/nature06119</ref> induce [[ferroelectricity]] in dielectrics,<ref>T. F. Nova, A. S. Disa, M. Fechner, and A. Cavalleri: ''Metastable ferroelectricity in optically strained SrTiO<sub>3</sub>.'' In:  ''Science'' 364 (6445), 1075-1079 (2019, DOI:  https://dx.doi.org/10.1126/science.aaw4911</ref> manipulate magnetism <ref>T. F. Nova, A. Cartella, A. Cantaluppi, M. Först, D. Bossini, R. V. Mikhaylovskiy, A. V. Kimel, R. Merlin, and A. Cavalleri: ''An effective magnetic field from optically driven phonons''. In: ''Nature Physics'' 13, 132-136 (2017), DOI:  https://dx.doi.org/10.1038/nphys3925</ref><ref>A. S. Disa, M. Fechner, T. F. Nova, B. Liu, M. Först, D. Prabhakaran, P. G. Radaelli, A. Cavalleri: ''Polarizing an antiferromagnet by optical engineering of the crystal field''. In: ''Nature Physics'' 16, 937-941 (2020), DOI:  https://dx.doi.org/10.1038/s41567-020-0936-3</ref>  and create non-equilibrium [[superconductivity]] at very high temperatures.<ref>D. Fausti, R. I. Tobey, N. Dean, S. Kaiser, A. Dienst, M. C. Hoffmann, S. Pyon, T. Takayama, H. Takagi, and A. Cavalleri: ''Light-Induced Superconductivity in a Stripe-Ordered Cuprate'' In: ''Science'' 331 (6014), 189-191 (2011), DOI: https://dx.doi.org/10.1126/science.1197294</ref><ref>M. Mitrano, A. Cantaluppi, D. Nicoletti, S. Kaiser, A. Perucchi, S. Lupi, P. Di Pietro, D. Pontiroli, M. Riccò, S. R. Clark, D. Jaksch, and A. Cavalleri: ''Possible light-induced superconductivity in K<sub>3</sub>C<sub>60</sub> at high temperature''. In: ''Nature'' 530, 461-464 (2016), DOI: https://dx.doi.org/10.1038/nature16522</ref> Cavalleri has also been amongst the people who applied the first [[femtosecond]] X-ray pulses to condensed matter systems, for example in his studies of photo-induced [[phase transition]]s.<ref>A. Cavalleri, Cs. Tóth, C. W. Siders, J. A. Squier, F. Ráksi, P. Forget, and J. C. Kieffer. ''Femtosecond Structural Dynamics in VO<sub>2</sub> during an Ultrafast Solid-Solid Phase Transition'' In: ''Physical Review Letters'' 87 (23), 237401 (2001), DOI:  https://dx.doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.237401</ref>

==Scientific career==
He received his laurea degree and PhD at the [[University of Pavia]], as a student of [[Collegio Borromeo|Almo Collegio Borromeo]], in 1994 and 1998 respectively. Cavalleri has held research positions at the [[University of Essen]], the [[University of California, San Diego]] and the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]].<ref>http://qcmd.mpsd.mpg.de/index.php/selected-publications-andrea-cavalleri.html Cavalleri's ''selected publications''</ref> In 2005, he joined the faculty of the University of Oxford, where he was promoted to Professor of Physics in 2006.<ref name="auto1"/> He joined the Max Planck Society in 2008.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.mpg.de/7067808/struktur_dynamik_materie_wissM|title=Cavalleri, Andrea|website=www.mpg.de}}</ref>

==Selected honors and awards==
He is a recipient of the 2004 [[European Science Foundation]] Young Investigator Award,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archives.esf.org/coordinating-research/euryi/awards/2004.html|title=2004 : European Science Foundation|website=archives.esf.org}}</ref> of the 2015 [[Max Born Medal]] from the [[Institute of Physics]] (UK)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iop.org/news/14/dec/page_64637.html|title=Born Medal and Prize for 2015 goes to Prof. Andrea Cavalleri|website=www.iop.org}}</ref> and the [[Deutsche Physikalische Gesellschaft]] and of the 2015 [[Dannie Heineman Prize (Göttingen)|Dannie Heineman Prize]] from the [[Gottingen Academy of Sciences|Göttingen Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mpsd.mpg.de/41210/2015-11-Akademiepreise|title=Göttinger Akademiepreise für Forscher des Hamburger Max-Planck-Instituts für Struktur und Dynamik der Materie|website=www.mpsd.mpg.de}}</ref> The [[American Physical Society]] awarded Cavalleri the 2018 [[Frank Isakson Prize for Optical Effects in Solids]] "''for pioneering contributions to the development and application of ultra-fast optical spectroscopy to condensed matter systems, and providing insight into lattice dynamics, structural phase transitions, and the non-equilibrium control of solids''".<ref name=":0" />  He is an elected fellow of the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>Mentioned from the APS in: https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Cavalleri&first_nm=Andrea&year=2018</ref> the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref>2016 AAAS Fellows approved by the AAAS Council DOI: https://dx.doi.org/10.1126/science.354.6315.981</ref> and the [[Institute of Physics]] (UK).<ref name="auto"/> He was elected a member of the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2017<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Cavalleri_Andrea|title=Academy of Europe: Cavalleri Andrea|website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref> and a fellow of the European Academy of Sciences in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurasc.org/user/63/andrea-cavalleri|title=European Academy of Sciences - Andrea Cavalleri|website=www.eurasc.org}}</ref>
